basis: User definition 2026-11-08: EconCS x blockchain x cryptography/security x OR/MS, finance, econ x systems. Any genuine crossing qualifies; pure single-side work and applications of the crossing to other domains do not. Extended 2026-11-08: formal methods count on the T side when combined with game theory/incentives (game theory + formal methods + systems/blockchain/security/crypto).

E.name: Economics / strategy side
covers: game theory, equilibrium, strategic or rational agents
mechanism, auction, market or contract design; incentive compatibility
incentives, rewards, fees, pricing, bribery, collusion, voting/governance with strategic analysis
microeconomics, industrial organization, monetary economics, finance (asset pricing, market microstructure, banking, lending)
OR/MS: optimization or stochastic models of strategic/economic behaviour, operations and information-systems economics
empirical economics/finance of a system (measured incentives, fees, prices, welfare, market structure)

T.name: Technical side
covers: blockchain, distributed ledgers, cryptocurrencies, smart contracts, DeFi, stablecoins, rollups, payment channels, consensus
cryptography and cryptographic protocols (MPC, secret sharing, commitments, ZK, fair exchange, encryption)
computer, network and system security; privacy; adversarial models
distributed, parallel, cloud-scheduler, peer-to-peer and database systems — when the system itself is the object of study
formal methods (verification, model checking, theorem proving, strategic/temporal logics) — when applied to strategic or incentive properties of protocols, systems or mechanisms

include_when: The paper has a real E x T crossing: an E-side element (model, theorem, mechanism, incentive analysis, economic measurement) applied to, or arising from, a T-side object that is itself the subject of the paper.

Topics that qualify: blockchain protocols with incentive/strategic analysis (including foundational protocols whose design rests on incentives, e.g. Bitcoin, Backbone with rewards, PoS); economics/finance of blockchains and crypto-assets; game theory or mechanism design for blockchain or cryptography; rational cryptography and rational adversaries; security games and the economics of security/attacks; game-theory- or mechanism-guided design of distributed/parallel/database/blockchain/cryptographic systems; DAO/on-chain governance with strategic analysis; MEV, transaction ordering and fee markets; AMMs/DEXs; staking, lending, liquidations, stablecoin design. Also: formal verification or model checking of game-theoretic/incentive properties (equilibria, incentive compatibility, rational behaviour) of blockchain, cryptographic, security or distributed protocols; rational verification; strategic logics and games on graphs used for such systems.
The crossing need not dominate the paper: a protocol paper with a genuine incentive-compatibility analysis, or an economics paper whose model is a blockchain/crypto system, both count.

exclude_when.rule: Pure cryptography, pure security, pure blockchain/systems engineering, consensus or performance work with no economic, strategic or incentive element. Formal verification of functional correctness or safety with no strategic/incentive element is single-side. An adversary, attacker or threat model is not by itself an E-side element: a security, consensus or attack paper qualifies only if it models or measures payoffs, costs, incentives, or rational/strategic behaviour.

Pure game theory, mechanism design, economics, finance or OR with no blockchain/crypto/security/systems object (e.g. generic auction theory, stock-market finance). Security is a T-side object, physical or computer: security games of any kind (Stackelberg security games, patrolling, network interdiction, attacker-defender and audit games), cybercrime and ransomware economics and cyber insurance qualify without any blockchain, and are neither single_side_E nor application_domain. This covers games between an attacker and a defender only; ordinary games, auctions and voting remain single_side_E.

The E x T machinery is applied to ANOTHER domain rather than studied in itself: IoT, edge/fog/mobile-edge computing, vehicular/UAV/satellite networks, wireless/spectrum/5G-6G resource allocation, smart grid and energy trading, healthcare, supply chain, agriculture, logistics, carbon credits, federated learning or crowdsourcing incentive schemes, metaverse services, e-government, education. Example to exclude: 'a game-theoretic blockchain incentive scheme for edge computing offloading'. Not this code: research on blockchain's economic impact on another sector, such as Bitcoin miners' electricity demand response to hashprice. It does apply to using blockchain to improve energy or other sectors, and to letting the grid or another sector guide blockchain design.
Crypto price/return prediction, technical trading or ML forecasting without an economic mechanism, market-structure or incentive question.

Tutorials, introductions, generic surveys, position pieces, editorials, book reviews. Exception: a systematization (SoK) at a peer-reviewed venue that organizes the E x T crossing itself. For a survey or SoK only, arXiv, SSRN and ePrint do not count as peer-reviewed venues. A paper with its own model, theorem, mechanism, data analysis or measurement is never no_contribution, and being a preprint or working paper is never a reason to exclude.
The E side is decorative: a game-theory or incentive word in the title but no model, no analysis and no measurable economic claim.

decisions.include: Clear crossing, in scope, not excluded.
decisions.exclude: One exclusion code applies (give the code).
decisions.needs_fulltext: Title/abstract are insufficient (missing or very short abstract, or crossing plausible but unclear). Never use for papers that are plainly out of scope.

topics.foundations: Foundational blockchain protocols/consensus whose design involves incentives or rational participants.
topics.mining: PoW mining incentives, selfish mining, pools, block withholding, difficulty/reward design.
topics.pos: Proof of stake, staking, validators, slashing and incentive security of PoS.
topics.tfm: Transaction fee mechanisms, fee markets, EIP-1559, blockspace pricing.
topics.mev: MEV, transaction ordering, PBS, sandwich/front-running, order-flow auctions.
topics.amm: Automated market makers, constant-function market makers, LP economics.
topics.defi: DeFi and financial economics of crypto assets: lending, liquidations, stablecoins, derivatives, crypto-asset pricing, banking.
topics.economics: Markets & platforms: market structure, platform/token economics not covered above, empirical blockchain economics.
topics.tokenomics: Token issuance, supply, monetary policy, adoption.
topics.economic-security: Attack costs, security budgets, bribery and economic security arguments.
topics.governance: DAO/on-chain governance with strategic or game-theoretic analysis.
topics.rational-cryptography: Rational cryptography, rational adversaries, security games, game-theoretic security and privacy (blockchain not required).
topics.incentive-systems: Game-theory- or mechanism-guided design of distributed, parallel, database or cryptographic systems outside the categories above. Includes formal verification of incentive/strategic properties of such systems.

prefilter.comment: Cheap, recall-oriented title/abstract regexes (case-insensitive). Pass = T_chain, or T_chain_weak unless the title is plainly from another field (T_chain_weak_noise) and has no economic word, or (E_strong and T_other), or (E_weak and T_strong). Venue rules widen the gate; general AI venues get no widening, and preprints need an E_specific term because a preprint server does not supply the T side (IACR ePrint is treated as Security & Crypto). Application-domain hints without a T_chain match are dropped as 'prefilter_application_domain'. Matching never authorizes inclusion; the LLM decides. Tuned 2026-11-09 against the directory and LLM includes; this does not change the version because no screening decision changes.

venue_rules.comment: Venue-aware widening. venue_group comes from data/venue_registry_v1.json.
